title: Link run request
description: The body of the session's POST to the run URL of its gateway's link, application/json, which opens a run: the run id the session chose, on the local link the run's labels and what the run is about, the session's images, and behind a separate gateway the session's narrowing of the policy. Behind a separate gateway the run id is the run key's, any other run_key_invalid, and labels or about are refused, invalid_request: the run's labels and about are the starter's registration's. A member this schema does not define is refused, invalid_request: a member the gateway does not read could be a narrowing it would drop.

version.description: The document format. The gateway refuses a version it does not read.

run_id.description: The run's id, which the session chooses on both transports: a UUID in the canonical lower-case form, the subject of every event of the run. Another form is invalid_request; an id that already names a run at this gateway, live or ended, is run_id_used.

wall.description: Whether the session runs the agent behind a wall. When it is true, the answer carries the run's image. The answer carries the run's certificate_authority when the gateway reads inside HTTPS for the run, with or without a wall.

labels.description: The run's labels, as dev.qory.run.started contains them: the run's. On the local link alone.

about.description: What the run is about, as dev.qory.run.started contains it. It selects no policy. On the local link alone.

images.description: The session's images, which the gateway resolves the policy's image selection against: the machine's default and the images the machine defines. A reference is not secret, but it may carry a registry's credentials in its user information: the gateway never logs or reports one. Absent means none.

default.description: The machine's default image: the name of one of definitions, or a reference, which starts under the engine's default runtime with no daemon. A name the definitions hold is read as that image first.

definitions.description: The images the machine defines, which a policy selects by name.

allow.description: The machine's images.allow: the prefixes of the references pinned by digest a policy may name its image by. An entry covers a reference that starts with it when the entry ends in / or @, or the reference's next character is / or @: registry.example/agents covers registry.example/agents/app@sha256:… and not registry.example/agents-other/app@sha256:…. Nothing is normalised. An entry that is not the start of a reference in lower case up to a whole part of it, and a list without a default, are refused, with no code. Absent means none: a policy names no image by reference.

narrowing.description: Behind a separate gateway alone, the session's narrowing of the policy the gateway holds for the run; on the local link it is invalid_request. It can only remove what the policy allows: allow, when present, removes every host it does not cover, and deny adds to the hosts denied. The lists have the grammar of the policy's egress.allow.

image.description: One image: its name, the reference, the container runtime the wall starts it under, whether it gives the agent nested Docker, and in an answer whether the policy named it by its reference.

name.description: What a policy, or the machine's default, selects it by. Absent for the machine's default given as a reference, and for an image the policy names by its reference.

ref.description: The image's reference, pinned by digest where the machine wants the same image every time. It may carry a registry's credentials in its user information: never logged or reported.

runtime.description: The container runtime the wall starts the image under, one the machine's engine has: sysbox-runc. Absent is the engine's default.

docker.description: True when the agent gets nested Docker, a Docker daemon inside the wall, separate from the machine's, which needs a runtime that runs one without privileges. Absent means false.

reference.description: In an answer alone: true when the policy named the image by its reference pinned by digest, under one of images.allow. Such an image starts under the default's runtime, with no nested Docker, as the wall's user; the wall fetches it, also when the engine holds it by that digest, and refuses one whose user is root, image_user_root; and the run's workspace is at /workspace inside. Absent means false.
